stemBlocks.value: Each of 75 girls named her favourite sport. The bar chart shows only two bars so far: track = 12 girls and cricket = 17 girls. (b) How many more girls chose cricket than track? (c) Eleven girls chose tennis; for the remaining girls the number choosing swimming to the number choosing football is in the ratio 2 : 3 — use this to complete the bar chart. (d) Determine the modal sport.
Think first: Read the two given bars off the chart, then treat the rest as a sharing-in-a-ratio problem on whatever girls are left.

solutionSteps.instruction: Read the two bars and subtract.
Find how many girls are left for swimming and football.
Share the 35 girls in the ratio 2 : 3.
Draw the three missing bars and compare all five frequencies.

contentBlocks.value: Swimming 14, tennis 11, track 12, cricket 17, football 21 — total 75
Result: Football has the highest bar

strategyBlocks.value: Take track = 12 and cricket = 17 from the chart, subtract track, cricket and tennis from 75 to find the girls left, share that remainder in the ratio 2 : 3, then compare all five totals for the mode.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (b) 5 more girls chose cricket than track.  (c) Remaining girls = 35, shared 2 : 3 gives swimming = 14 and football = 21, so bars of height 14 (swimming), 11 (tennis) and 21 (football) complete the chart.  (d) The modal sport is football (21 girls).

whyThisWorks.value: The five bars must account for all 75 girls, so once three of the groups are known the rest is a fixed remainder. Sharing that remainder in the ratio 2 : 3 means splitting it into 5 equal parts and giving two parts to swimming and three to football. The mode is simply the category that occurs most often — on a bar chart, the tallest bar.

commonErrors.misconception: Sharing all 75 girls in the ratio 2 : 3 instead of only the 35 who are left.
